items.hint: Ask two questions before you compute: exactly what is being squared, and what does the minus in front of the bracket do to each term inside it?
worked: Nothing brackets the $-3$, so the exponent binds first: $-3^{2}=-(3^{2})=-9$.

items.stem: Exactly one of the four statements below is always true. Which statement is true?
items.hint: Rewrite every minus sign in front of a bracket as $-1$ times that bracket, and test any statement you are unsure of with a single easy number such as $x=1$.
worked: $-(3-x)=-1\cdot 3+(-1)(-x)=-3+x$, and $-3+x$ is the same as $x-3$, so that statement is true.
$-(x-7)=-x+7$, not $-x-7$: the minus must reach the second term too.
$-6^{2}$ means $-(6^{2})=-36$, not $36$; only a bracket around $-6$ would give $36$.
$(x+5)^{2}=(x+5)(x+5)=x^{2}+10x+25$, so the middle term is missing from $x^{2}+25$.

items.hint: Expand the square first and keep the result inside its bracket, then hand out the leading minus sign to every term you find there.
worked: The leading minus applies to all three terms: $-(x^{2}+10x+25)=-x^{2}-10x-25$.
